---
title: Desktop installer (plan)
---

This page is a plan for shipping the Nostalgia Index app as a desktop installer (`.dmg`, `.exe`, `.AppImage`) with the [shinyelectron](https://r-pkg.thecoatlessprofessor.com/shinyelectron/) R package (version 0.2.1 or later). Nothing described here exists in the repository yet.

shinyelectron only understands an app directory (a folder with an `app.py`). The package is not an app directory, so the plan generates a thin launcher folder that imports the package, vendors a copy of the package next to it, and hands that folder to `shinyelectron::export()`. The package source stays as it is.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":true}}}%%
flowchart TD
    PKG["src/nostalgia_index/"] --> SC(["scaffold_py.py"])
    SC --> APP["electron/app/"]
    APP --> CHK(["app_check()"])
    CHK --> EXP(["export()"])
    EXP --> DIST["electron/dist/electron-app/dist/"]
```

## Entry point

The app already exposes a module level `App` object, so no source changes are needed.

```python
# src/nostalgia_index/app/app.py
app = App(app_ui, server, static_assets=Path(__file__).parent / "www")
```

The launcher imports it from `nostalgia_index.app.app`. `run_app()` is not used, because shinyelectron owns the port and the server process. The app name and version (`nostalgia_index`, `0.1.0`) come from `[project]` in `pyproject.toml`.

## Build machine

shinyelectron is an R package, so the build machine needs R (4.4 or later) and Node (22 or later, with npm 11.5 or later). End users need neither.

```r
shinyelectron::sitrep_shinyelectron()
shinyelectron::install_nodejs()   # only if Node is missing
```

## Runtime strategy

The plan uses the `bundled` strategy, which ships a portable Python with the installer (roughly 150 to 300 MB). The other strategies were ruled out for these reasons:

* `shinylive`: `httpx` cannot open sockets inside Pyodide, and `diskcache` relies on SQLite file locking. The app could not reach the Wikimedia API.
* `system`: it requires users to have Python on their `PATH`.
* `container`: there are no heavy system libraries to justify Docker.
* `auto-download`: it is a reasonable fallback if installer size becomes a problem, since the app needs internet access anyway.

The app is never fully offline. Every index computation calls the Wikimedia REST API, so the installer removes the Python requirement, not the network requirement.

## Scaffold the launcher

Run the scaffold script from the package root. It is idempotent and should be re-run before every build to refresh the vendored copy.

```bash
python tools/scaffold_py.py \
  --strategy=bundled \
  --module=nostalgia_index.app.app \
  --attr=app \
  --platforms=mac,win,linux
```

It creates the following files:

```
electron/
├── app/
│   ├── app.py               # from nostalgia_index.app.app import app
│   ├── requirements.txt     # [project].dependencies
│   ├── nostalgia_index/     # vendored copy (gitignored)
│   └── _shinyelectron.yml   # name, version, strategy, dependencies
└── build.R                  # app_check() + export() into electron/dist
```

Two repository changes go with it. `electron/dist/` and `electron/app/nostalgia_index/` are added to `.gitignore`, and `electron/` is excluded from the sdist.

```toml
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
exclude = ["electron"]
```

## Dependency checks

* `shinywidgets` and `plotly`: these are pure Python and install from `requirements.txt` into the bundled runtime.
* `custom.css`: it is resolved with `Path(__file__).parent`, so it loads from the vendored copy regardless of the working directory.
* Cache: `diskcache` writes to `~/.cache/nostalgia_index` (or `NOSTALGIA_CACHE_DIR`). This resolves on all three platforms, but the Windows path should be confirmed in a test build.
* User-Agent: `USER_AGENT` in `client.py` still holds placeholder contact details. These must be real before a public release (see [Ethics and rate limits](03-ethics-and-rate-limits.qmd)).
* Python pin: set `dependencies.python.version` in `_shinyelectron.yml` to a version that satisfies `requires-python >= 3.10`.

## Validate and build

```bash
Rscript electron/build.R
```

`build.R` runs `app_check("electron/app")` and then `export()`. Only the contents of `electron/dist/electron-app/dist/` get shipped. If the packaged app fails to start, launch it with `SHINYELECTRON_DEBUG=1` to see runtime detection, dependency installs, and server startup.

## Signing and CI

macOS installers only build on macOS, and `bundled` cannot cross-build, so each platform builds on its own CI runner.

* Copy `build-installers.yml` from the py-shinyelectron-pkg skill assets into `.github/workflows/`, and copy `scaffold_py.py` into `tools/` (the workflow calls it there).
* Signing uses `sign = TRUE` with the `CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`, and `APPLE_TEAM_ID` secrets. Secrets go in the job level `env:` block, never in files.
* Trigger the workflow on version tags so the installer version tracks `pyproject.toml`.

## Checklist

```
- [ ] Preflight the build machine (R, Node, npm)
- [ ] Add tools/scaffold_py.py and run it with --strategy=bundled
- [ ] Update .gitignore and the hatch sdist exclude
- [ ] Pin dependencies.python.version
- [ ] Replace the placeholder User-Agent contact details
- [ ] Run electron/build.R locally and test the installer
- [ ] Confirm the cache path on Windows
- [ ] Add the CI workflow and signing secrets
```

## Version bumps

The installer version is pinned to the package version. Bump `version` in `pyproject.toml` and re-run the scaffold; never edit the version in `_shinyelectron.yml` by hand.
